$comment: D16: this is a data file, not a script constant, so it is reviewable as a diff and no code path can extend it. Every entry below was measured on the workspace at frozenAt. Nothing in this repository writes this file: ui/scripts/verify-ui.mjs, scripts/check-ui-conformance.sh and tests/Platform.Architecture.Tests/UiDistributionTests.cs only read it, and the guard fails with ui-legacy-list-grew if divergentPrimitive grows.

The list is closed and can only shrink. A repository that migrates leaves the list; there is no flag, comment or argument anywhere that adds an entry. The purpose of a closed list is that the sixteenth copy - the one this change actually exists to stop - fails, while the fifteen already written stay visible and block nothing today.

D17: arivio is migrationOrder 1 because its copy is a measured accessibility defect, not a style disagreement. It omits padding, margin and border, so a screen-reader-only element still occupies a 1x1px box. Repositories that are only stylistically divergent may wait for their own schedule (follow-up change ui-fleet-adoption).

The three baseline sections are the same mechanism applied to the three things a consumer could newly get wrong: declaring a shared primitive itself, shipping UI with no declaration at all, and introducing a width-based media query value that is not the kit scale. All three are frozen because all three exist today; none of them may grow.

divergentPrimitive.divergence: omits padding, margin and border from the reset, so the element leaks a 1x1px box
every declaration is !important, so a consumer cascade cannot override it
position is !important while the other eight declarations are not
compound selector and no white-space: nowrap, so long content can wrap into the layout
uses border-width: 0 where the canonical rule uses border: 0
canonical body plus a focusable variant the shared layer does not ship
space-separated clip: rect(0 0 0 0) rather than the comma form
comma-form clip; body otherwise matches the canonical rule

$undeclaredUiComment: Repositories that ship a user interface (a .razor/.cshtml/.html/.vue/.svelte/.jsx/.tsx file, or a stylesheet under a web/wwwroot/frontend/client/ui/app/site/src/public/assets path) and declare no ui-conformance.json. Frozen so the check can start from a truthful baseline: a new UI-bearing repository with no declaration fails ui-conformance-undeclared, these do not. It can only shrink.
$flutterComment: NG5: the platform ships no Dart token artifact, so these repositories are reported as not covered and are never failed. forge's own scaffold declares flutter-app: tokens: none for the same reason.

kitScale.$comment: The documented platform responsive scale. A width-based media query may use one of these values with no declaration; any other value is either baselined below (it predates this capability) or fails ui-breakpoint-undeclared.

$mediaQueryComment: Distinct width-based media query values present in the workspace at frozenAt, with their occurrence and file counts. 640px/641px and 768px/769px are the off-by-one pairs: they are the same nominal breakpoint written two ways, they predate this capability, and the check reports them as known divergence without failing.
